subject: Pathfinder launch remedy — request for timeboxed rate relief / one-off credit
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pathfinder launch remedy — request for timeboxed rate relief / one-off credit

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Quick background: Pathfinder (D-83421) was planning a full launch for their enterprise search product on Nov 1. We hit a blocker — multi-model inference (their configuration needs longseq + multi-model routing) was not available in our preferred region on the originally promised ship date. Customer has paused onboarding and is requesting commercial remediation tied to the delay.

What sales is asking: a timeboxed rate relief (one-off credit) to cover the revenue shortfall they claim from a missed launch window while we complete the quant rollout. They propose a ~12% credit on committed usage for the first 3 months post-launch (~$42k estimate).

Why this is product's problem: the rollout of longseq multi-model kernels was delayed by two weeks due to quant integration and test regressions. Karthik — we understand engineering is expediting the patches but the customer needs a concrete commercial gesture to proceed.

Attached: Pathfinder_MAAP_v2.pdf (customer MAAP/ask), usage snapshot, and a short proposed-credit-term brief.

Ask: 1) Exec approval for a timeboxed one-off credit (12% for 3 months) or an alternative (temporary rate cap at X tokens/price) we can offer immediately, 2) if approved, who should sign the DocuSign and 3) product ETA commitment we can promise in writing to close the loop.

I recommend approving a capped one-off credit (not a permanent price change) tied to a launch milestone; this keeps the deal but limits long-term precedent. Sales is standing by — Nina at Pathfinder is expecting an answer this week.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment stubs: Pathfinder_MAAP_v2.pdf (proposal), pathfinder-usage-snapshot-20281118.csv (billing sample), proposed-credit-term-brief.docx (internal memo)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-19T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Pathfinder launch remedy — request for timeboxed rate relief / one-off credit

Soojin — thanks for the context and the attachments. I pulled the postmortem notes from the quant rollout: the delay was caused by an unexpected divergence in longseq attention kernels when combined with our new KV-cache packing on the AmpX nodes. Engineering has a patch in validation, ETA production rollout is 11/27.

Questions/notes:
- Is the requested credit tied to absolute dollars or to a post-launch adoption milestone (e.g., 3 months of committed usage at >= 60% of forecast)? Tying it to adoption reduces moral hazard.
- Product can commit to a target: production flip + monitoring dashboard by 11/27 and a bi-weekly sync for the first 6 weeks post-launch to ensure perf stays within SLOs.
- If sales wants the credit sooner, we should scope it as a "launch safeguard" — timeboxed and conditional on the production flip.

I support a conditional one-off credit if it's tied to a clear milestone and a sunset clause. LMK the exact numbers and I'll add the prod commitment language to the DocuSign memo.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
VP, Serving & Product Reliability
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-11-20T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Pathfinder launch remedy — request for timeboxed rate relief / one-off credit

Team — brief customer context from my side: Pathfinder is a high-value trial (projected 18-month ARR $1.2M if successful). They delayed launch primarily because internal infra flagged performance variability during heavy multi-model traffic. They are willing to sign if we provide an immediate commercial signal; their procurement lead (Nina) says the finance committee will greenlight the SOW with a short-term remediation written into the contract.

My proposal: approve a one-off credit capped at $45k, disbursed as a 3-month rebate contingent on production-ready longseq availability and meeting a simple adoption check (>= 55% of forecasted token usage in month 2). If we agree, Finance can route this through the commercial make-good budget; legal can add the clause to the SOW.

Marissa — can you confirm if we have headroom in the make-good budget for a $45k cap? Also tagging Karthik for the production commitment language.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of North America Sales, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Marissa — looping you to get final exec sign-off. Updated ask per thread: approve a conditional one-off credit, capped at $45k, paid as a 3-month rebate. Conditions: (1) production longseq rollout in region by 2028-11-27, (2) adoption milestone >=55% forecast in month 2, (3) clause sunsets after the 3-month rebate window. Karthik will add the production commitment language.

If approved, next steps: 1) Marissa signs the brief approval memo and we attach to the SOW, 2) Legal adds the conditional rebate clause, 3) Finance pushes funding from commercial make-good. I've prepopulated the DocuSign draft: https://docusign.example.com/rooms/XX-Pathfinder-83421

Customer-facing line (for Nina): "Redwood will provide a time-limited launch safeguard in the form of a one-time, conditional commercial rebate (capped at $45k) tied to product availability and adoption milestones. This rebate does not change standard pricing after the rebate window."

Please reply-all with APPROVE or REJECT and any edits to the covenant language. If I don't hear back by EOD tomorrow (11/23), I'll escalate to commercial leadership.

Thanks — Soojin
